payload.title: [multi-region-1] Federated RegionEnvelopes cross the WAN with zero authentication — a rogue/compromised region (...
payload.description:
AUDIT FINDING multi-region-1 (critical/authz, confidence=high, verify-votes +2/-0)

FILE: apps/server/src/cluster/region-redis-bus.ts
LINES: 86-108, 110-124

WHAT: RedisRegionBus.#onMessage decodes a msgpack RegionEnvelope off the shared cross-region pub/sub channel (default `frick:region`) and, after only the `originRegionId === this.regionId` loop guard, hands `envelope` straight to every subscriber. The sole subscriber is FederatingClusterBus (region-bus.ts:223-225), which re-injects `regionEnvelope.envelope` verbatim into the LOCAL cluster bus via `this.#local.publish(...)`. That envelope flows into the gateway's #handleClusterEnvelope (gateway.ts:849-902), which fans it out to local WebSocket subscribers purely on the strength of the envelope's self-asserted `tenantId` — no signature, HMAC, nonce, or per-region credential is ever checked (confirmed: no `hmac|sign|verify|auth|secret|token` anywhere in any region file). The inner ClusterEnvelope union includes streamEvent/objects/objectDeletes/signal/projectionDelta/presenceDelta, so a single forged frame on the WAN channel forges a stream event, deletes objects, or spoofs presence for ANY tenant in EVERY region that subscribes. The intra-region Redis bus has the same property, but that is a single trust domain; FR-105/FR-157 extend the exact same unauthenticated trust across a WAN boundary while the module docs claim federation merely 'carries cluster envelopes ACROSS regions' without ever documenting that this assumes a fully-trusted, mutually-authenticated inter-region transport.

IMPACT: Cross-tenant data forgery and leakage across the entire mesh: any party able to PUBLISH to the cross-region channel (a compromised region node, a misconfigured/shared Redis, a leaked Redis credential, or a malicious peer operator in a federated deployment) can inject object deletes, fake stream events, spoofed presence, and signals for arbitrary tenants in every region. Tenant isolation — the core multi-tenant security guarantee — does not survive federation.

SUGGESTED FIX: Authenticate the cross-region transport at the application layer, not just by trusting the network: add a per-deployment shared secret and attach an HMAC over the encoded RegionEnvelope (and a monotonic/nonce field for replay resistance), verified in #onMessage before any handler dispatch; drop+log frames that fail. At minimum, document in region-redis-bus.ts and docs/multi-region.md that the region channel MUST run over a mutually-authenticated, tenant-trusted transport (mTLS, dedicated private network, per-region ACLs) and that the channel is a cross-tenant trust boundary. Optionally validate that an inbound envelope's tenant is one this region is authorized to host before re-injecting.
